headline: Messi scores and assists twice as Argentina wins 3-0 in his farewell match
summary: Lionel Messi marked his final match for Argentina with a goal and two assists in a dominant 3-0 victory over Benin at the Estadio Monumental, concluding his international career with a memorable performance.
details: Lionel Messi's final match for Argentina saw him score a goal and provide two assists, leading the team to a dominant 3-0 victory over Benin. The football legend concluded his international career with a memorable performance at Buenos Aires' Estadio Monumental.

The match, held on Wednesday (October 7), saw Argentina dominate possession from the start. Despite early attacks, the Albiceleste forwards struggled to break through Benin's defense in the first half, which ended in a goalless draw.

A special moment occurred in the 10th minute when the referee paused the game for about 90 seconds to honor Messi. Fans in the stadium gave a standing ovation, chanting "Ole Ole Messi" to celebrate the superstar.
The deadlock was broken in the 48th minute when Nicolás Otamendi scored from a Messi corner. Messi then provided his second assist in the 61st minute, setting up Nico Paz for Argentina's second goal.

Messi himself converted a penalty in the 71st minute after Agustín Giay was fouled in the box, extending Argentina's lead to 3-0. This goal sealed his perfect farewell performance for the national team.

Messi concludes his illustrious career with Argentina having played 208 matches and scored 126 goals, including World Cup and Copa América titles. His profound impact on Argentine football extends far beyond mere statistics.

headline_marked: [[48,000+ mosquito control committees exist only on paper]] nationwide, dengue deaths reach 281
headline: 48,000+ mosquito control committees exist only on paper nationwide, dengue deaths reach 281
summary: Despite over 48,000 committees formed to combat dengue, most remain inactive, contributing to a surge in cases. Bangladesh has recorded 281 dengue deaths this year, with experts highlighting the Local Government Ministry's lack of initiative.
details: Over 48,000 committees, established to control mosquitoes and prevent dengue across Bangladesh, exist only on paper and are inactive in reality. This alarming revelation comes as dengue cases continue to surge, with the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reporting 281 deaths this year.

The dengue outbreak has now spread to all districts of the country. The primary responsibility for controlling Aedes mosquitoes, the vector for dengue, lies with the Local Government Division of the Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development, and Cooperatives.

A 2019 'National Guideline for Prevention of Dengue and Other Mosquito-Borne Diseases' by the Local Government Division mandated the formation of committees from the union level up to the national level. These guidelines detailed the composition, formation dates, and scope of work for each committee.

However, most of these committees, particularly at the district, upazila, and union levels, are virtually inactive. Only the national committee and those in the 13 city corporations are reportedly functional.

Joint Secretary of the Local Government Division, Md. Rabiul Islam, stated that national and city corporation committees are working on mosquito control. He also claimed that the 330 municipal committees are active, and other committees are 'surely active' and working.

Despite these claims, the lowest-tier committees, the 'Dengue and Other Mosquito-Borne Disease Prevention Committees' at the union ward level (41,391 wards across 4,599 unions), are reportedly non-existent. There is no known instance of such a committee being active.

In total, 48,559 committees were supposed to be formed under the Local Government Division. Many officials are unaware of the existence of such a vast network of committees, with one researcher advising the government on dengue stating that union or ward-level committees are not discussed in policy meetings.

The 2019 guideline clearly outlines the Local Government Division's role in coordinating all stakeholders, providing guidance and support to local government institutions for year-round dengue prevention activities, and monitoring their implementation. They are also responsible for taking necessary actions based on feedback from all levels.

The national committee is tasked with reviewing, evaluating, monitoring, and coordinating implemented activities, conducting research, and formulating policies and strategies. It is mandated to hold at least four meetings annually.

Detailed responsibilities are also outlined for city corporations, district committees, municipal committees, and upazila committees, including monthly meetings and implementing legal measures like mobile courts to destroy mosquito breeding grounds.
